messages.author: bba8ce58a28a6363
messages.subject: recordTable warning: omitting images because of missing/unreadable date/time information
parts:
Greetings,

When running recordTable with the following call I get the warning "omitting X images because of missing/unreadable date/time information":

recordtable<- recordTable(inDir = "E:/2018_tagged", 
                        IDfrom = "metadata", 
                        camerasIndependent = T, 
                        minDeltaTime = 1, 
                        deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord", 
                        metadataSpeciesTag = "Species", 
                        timeZone = "America/Los_Angeles")

Warning: 14 : omitting 2 images because of missing/unreadable date/time information.

The warnings only happen for certain folders. For the purposes of troubleshooting, is there a way to find out which images were omitted? 

Or better yet, is there a solution for this?

Please let me know if more information is needed.

Thank you,
Joel

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: recordTable warning: omitting images because of missing/unreadable date/time information
parts:
Hi Joel,
the function does not return this information. It might be a good idea to add that. The function tells you that the problem is in station 14 though.

In the meantime, maybe digiKam or some other image viewer/editor can help? In digikam see the left side, the Dates or Timeline menus.

Alternatively, use the terminal (cmd.exe) and run exiftool directly on that folder:

exiftool -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal E:/2018_tagged/14

The 14 is just a guess about your folder name. Replace the path with whatever it is on your hard disk,

You should be able to spot which one is the cuprit (it may be a hassle though with many images).

Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: recordTable warning: omitting images because of missing/unreadable date/time information
parts:
Mabel,
is it only a few images or a systematic problem with all of these cameras? Feel free to share the message the function returns.

A few things you can try to identify the problem: 
- see if digiKam or other image management software can read the date/time tag
- run exifTagNames(..., returnMetadata = TRUE) on the faulty images to see the metadata.
- if it is troublesome to copy the faulty images into a directory as required for exifTagNames, upload the image to this webiste to see the metadata: https://exifmeta.com/. See the field ExifIFD:DateTimeOriginal. It should be something like 2015:02:23 21:37:59
- if none of this helps, share a sample image here 

Hope this helps,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: recordTable warning: omitting images because of missing/unreadable date/time information
parts:
Hi Mabel, 
glad you got it to run. 
Regarding video metadata support, as far as I know is implemented in digiKam since version 6.0. I haven't tried it, as I was under the impression that the metadata are still inconsistent in video files. How are your experiences with the video files, can you get the date/time information of the videos out with exiftool? That is the crucial bit of information that is lost so easily I decided not to include video support (even though exiftool can read video metadata without problems). Would you mind sharing a sample video please (in a zip file, so the video metadata are not stripped when you upload here)?
To sum up, currently camtrapR does not have any video support. Video files should be ignored while camtrapR reads information from JPG files normally. Do I understand correctly that camtrapR does not work if there is more than just JPG files in the folders? Can you provide more details please? That would need to be fixed. 
All the best,
Jürgen
